newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: ASEAN mediation team set to return to Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN mediation team set to return to Cambodia.

text.p: An Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) mediation team will arrive in Phnom Penh on Saturday to resume efforts to help restore political stability in the strife-torn country, government officials said on Friday.

Second Prime Minster Hun Sen, who ousted his co-premier on July 6 and subsequently rejected ASEAN efforts to mediate in the crisis, will meet the three-member team on Saturday morning, an aide to Hun Sen said.

Cambodia was scheduled to join ASEAN in late July, but the grouping postponed Cambodia's membership indefinitely in response to Hun Sen's bloody overthrow on July 6 of his senior coalition partner, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

The officials said the ASEAN team due on Saturday would be made up of the same men who flew to Phnom Penh and tried unsuccessfully to launch a mediation effort two weeks ago -- foreign ministers Ali Alatas of Indonesia, Prachuab Chaiyasan of Thailand and Domingo Siazon of the Philippines.
Cambodia's troubles dominated a recent ASEAN foreign ministers' meeting in Kuala Lumpur.
The grouping was thrown into confusion by conflicting signals from Cambodia over whether or not the Hun Sen-controlled government would welcome a mediation effort.
Foreign Minister Ung Huot said in Kuala Lumpur last month that Cambodia wanted ASEAN to help mediate, but Hun Sen later said Cambodia's problems should be solved internally.
Hun Sen said ASEAN's role in ensuring Cambodia's stability should be limited to preventing foreign interference in Cambodia's affairs.
But after ASEAN requested clarification on the issue, Ung Huot wrote to the group on behalf of Hun Sen, inviting the three foreign ministers back to Phnom Penh for talks.
"I have the pleasure to reconfirm that Cambodia welcomes ASEAN's role to help restore political stability to the country," Ung Huot said in his letter on Tuesday.
ASEAN currently comprises Brunei, Burma, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
